patterns: Alaska's same-name scheme was the day's biggest story line: 13 hits (~569k) on Peltola, Alaska or 'Dan Sullivan', led by rawsalerts' NYT spoiler-candidate report (~137k) and Gunther's 'subpoenas coming' (~147k); Gunther's 'caught red-handed' framing earned the best like rate of the bunch at 11.5%

Fraud and lawfare stayed a reliable engine: 10 hits (~505k) mention fraud or scams, with the Feeding Our Future 30-year sentence at 12.3% likes and the O'Keefe and Higby felony charges at 7.5%; alx echoed the O'Keefe angle (~21k, his best like count)
Omar and Somali-credentials posts reached wide: 8 hits (~445k), led by the 'fake ID and fake credentials' line (~243k at 12.1%), plus the sealed raid warrant and judge twist (~72k and ~63k)

Faith and short moral one-liners again earned the most loyalty: Charlie Kirk's truth quote (13.4%), 'Tim Walz should be prosecuted' (17.3%), and 'My kind of people vote RED' (8.8%) all beat the long breaking-news posts on like rate

Election framing was the base layer: 55 hits (~1.56M) mention voting, ballots, polls or the midterms, from Trump's 'the choice is clear' (~47k) to Nicki Minaj backing Blakeman (~35k at 11.1%) and Cuban Americans voting Republican (~35k)

Reach without love: the vague 'I bet he's a Democrat' post (~480k at 0.9%), the Savannah River nuclear-site fire (~63k at 1.5%) and the Texas softball brawl (~50k at 2.5%) went wide but earned few likes
Halloween is starting to show up: the superhero-costume kindness post (~48k at 7.2%) and 'dress up as ICE' (~43k) were the first seasonal hits
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, two searches, about 50 posts) was dominated by money and infrastructure rather than products. The biggest items were @business on Marvell's advanced talks to buy optics maker Lumentum (~35k) and on a shortage of the largest warehouses for data center builders (~26k), plus SoftBank planning $50B for data centers and AI in Malaysia (~9k). Smaller threads covered Microsoft offering 60,000 buyouts while leaning on AI agents, Barclays seeking insurance on $10B+ of AI infrastructure loans, OpenAI and Anthropic both claiming their models cracked the Exponential Time Hypothesis, and AI agents breaking into Anthropic through vendor tools. Free 'learn AI' course lists were the only creator-style posts getting traction. None of the outsiders came close to the watchlist's reach.
narrative_synthesis: A steady weekday window: 165 hits and ~5.6M views from 165 originals, up from ~4.7M yesterday, with rawsalerts back (two originals, including the day's top post on Harvard enrollment at ~720k). Gunther carried volume on Alaska's same-name scheme, Omar, fraud sentencings and the Brooklyn Bridge sit-in, while short moral one-liners and faith posts earned the best like rates (9-17%). The playbook for a creator riding this: turn the scandal of the day into a useful, calm action step for voters and families, and keep the short sincere posts coming; vague bait gets reach but not loyalty.
